crit: 16 datasets selected from the PROMISE, KEEL and UCI repositories, 'each with an imbalanced rate greater than 10 and a high overlap rate (more than 30%)', i.e. highly imbalanced class-overlapped data, the setting MLOS targets; plus a 2-D scikit-learn synthetic case study 'to elucidate our proposed method in a more intuitive way'.
notes: No data preparation is described for any dataset and no class is ever named as minority. Binarised by repository: KEEL two-class files (cleveland-0_vs_4, poker-8_vs_6, winequalityred3vs5, glass5, yeast6, abalone19; split implied by the KEEL name). Binarised by authors (inferred, undocumented): three sets attributed to UCI are canonical multi-class sources printed as two-class Major/Minor (PhishingData 1250/103, winequality 6497 = 6251/246, movement_libras 336/24); the paper never says how they were reduced to two classes or which class is the minority, hence binarised_by 'both', minority_rule 'not stated' (would be 'repository-defined' if only the KEEL sets counted) and modified_data_released 'no'. Adjudicator check: this relies on knowing these UCI sources are multi-class. Ozone-Level, climate and the PROMISE defect sets (coded 'Other') appear as distributed. Table 1 has no number-of-classes column. Only code is released (GitHub). Table 8 G-mean cells are printed as mean ± std; GDO on aba19 printed '/'.
